commits.message:
fix(hero): eliminate load-time layout shift and stale role text (#103)

CLS on load was about 0.44 (desktop) and 0.31-0.44 (mobile), all from the hero:

- ui.js still ran a legacy typing effect that, after 1s, overwrote
  .hero-subtitle with hard-coded old roles ("Full-Stack Developer", ...),
  deleting the data-roles span and caret that hero-text.js animates.
  Remove it.
- The role typewriter changed the subtitle's height as roles wrapped
  and unwrapped. Reserve the tallest role's height, and re-measure on
  resize.
- The name scramble used narrower glyphs, which reflowed the centred
  heading every frame and sometimes dropped a line. Render each glyph
  in a fixed-width cell (per-word nowrap) and hold the heading height
  until it settles.

CLS is now 0.000 on load at 1280x800 and 390x844.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(activity): restore commit messages and PR titles in activity events (#102)

GitHub's events API no longer includes commit lists in PushEvent
payloads or titles in PullRequestEvent payloads, so the activity feed
and the "currently coding" widget fell back to generic text.

- Data workflow: fill both back in from the commit and PR endpoints
  (de-duplicated, best effort) before writing github-data.json.
- Worker: pick the event first, then fill in only that one (one extra
  subrequest, still edge-cached for 5 minutes).

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ci): drop broken metrics plugins, make plugin errors fatal (#101)

The activity and habits plugins read commit lists from PushEvent
payloads, which GitHub's events API no longer returns. Both crashed on
every run, and since plugin errors were non-fatal the job reported
success while committing a github-metrics.svg with two 'Unexpected
error' boxes. Remove both plugins and set plugins_errors_fatal so a
broken plugin fails the run instead of shipping a broken image.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

comment.diff_hunk:
@@ -155,8 +155,11 @@ create_backup() {
             exit 1
         fi
     else
-        echo -e "${RED}Backup creation failed (tar exit ${tar_status}, gzip exit ${gzip_status})${NC}"
-        grep -v -i "memory.*limit" "$tar_log" | tail -20 || true
+        # stderr, because that is what POST /api/backup returns on failure
comment.body: You are right on both counts. In `create_backup` two of the three failure exits still wrote to stdout only: the failed integrity check (which also left the unreadable archive in `backups/`) and the missing-data-directory exit you pointed at. Fixed in db8bbb5: both messages now go to stderr, and an archive that fails the integrity check is removed so it cannot show up in the list of backups the panel offers to restore. Two new Bats tests cover them (the stub can now emit a non-tar stream with exit 0, so only the integrity check can tell); both fail against the previous script.

comment.diff_hunk:
@@ -239,6 +242,20 @@ All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- **A failed backup now tells the admin panel why** — `scripts/manage.sh` printed the
+  `tar`/`gzip` diagnostics on stdout, but `POST /api/backup` returns only stderr when the
+  script fails, so the panel showed a failure with no reason. The failure message and
+  the last lines of the `tar` log now go to stderr. (Found in review of #76 and pushed
comment.body: You are right, and it is wider than the comment says. The response interceptor passes Axios errors through untouched, and `useErrorHandler` took `err.message` first, which an Axios error always has, so the API's reason never reached the toast on any page that uses the hook. The existing test fed it a plain object with no `message`, so it could not see this. Fixed in db8bbb5: the hook now prefers `err.response.data.error`, then `err.message`, then the caller's default. New tests use a real `AxiosError` carrying both fields (the API reason must show, the generic text must not) and a network error with no response (still shows its message). The first fails against the old precedence. I also rewrote the changelog entry so it says exactly what is now true.

commits.message:
fix(backup): report every failure on stderr, and show the API's reason in the panel

Review of #108. create_backup still wrote two of its three failure messages to
stdout (no data directory; failed integrity check), which POST /api/backup never
returns, and left an unreadable archive in backups/. useErrorHandler preferred
err.message, which an Axios error always has, over the reason the API returned,
so the panel showed 'Request failed with status code 500'.

@@ -57,3 +57,11 @@ description = "Bare PEM header in the Apple OAuth instructions, with no key mate
 condition = "AND"

+
+[[allowlists]]
+description = "Python tool caches: gitignored and rebuilt on demand, so a working-tree scan has no business in them. A type checker's cache of a test file repeats that file's made-up credentials, which is all that was ever found here."

comment.body: You are right, and thank you for the pointer to the header. I had checked the new block with my local gitleaks (8.30.1), where it works; the pinned 8.24.3 ignores it. I re-ran it against that exact binary (Docker, with the real cache file): the top-level block left all three findings in place. A scanner-level `[allowlist]` fixed them on 8.24.3 but newer gitleaks refuses to load the config with it next to the existing `[[allowlists]]`, so I did not use that either. The paths now sit in `generic-api-key`'s own `[rules.allowlist]`, the rule that fires and the form this file already uses. Verified on both: 8.24.3 no longer reports the cache file and still flags the same token in a normal path, and `make secrets` passes on 8.30.1. The remaining 8.24.3 finding on the whole repo is the existing `docs/OAUTH_SETUP.md` top-level block, which this change does not touch.

chore(web): upgrade to Tailwind CSS 4 (#106)

Done with the official upgrade tool, then checked page by page. The theme moves
to an @theme block in index.css and PostCSS uses @tailwindcss/postcss. The tool
left bg-opacity-* (removed in 4), which becomes the slash form, and put the
global rules in @layer utilities, which becomes @layer base. Tailwind 4's changed
defaults are restored so nothing changes visually: fixed default line heights,
the gray placeholder color and the pointer cursor on buttons, plus an explicit
lg:leading-8 on the login heading. All snapshots pass and a comparison of 24
routes against Tailwind 3 shows no difference above 3/255 per channel.

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
chore(ci): make make ci about twice as fast (#105)

* chore(ci): run the BATS suite in parallel and alongside the other make ci steps

The suite was 157 of make ci's 231 seconds, one file after another. The files
now run in parallel with per-file buffered output, and make ci runs the suite
in the background while the other steps run (about 111 seconds in total).
Results are named by position, the temp directory is removed on every exit
path, an xargs failure is reported, and an early failure stops the suite's
whole process tree without job control (set -m is not portable to dash/ash).
BATS_JOBS and CI_SERIAL tune or disable it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(ci): CI_SERIAL=1 runs the BATS suite after the fast checks, as before

Serial mode ran the suite first, so it delayed finding an early lint failure
and did not match the order the docs describe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
